The total concentration and speciation of Cu (3-44 nM), Pb (0.1-0.8 nM) and Zn (9-300 nM) were determined by square-wave anodic stripping voltammerty (SWASV), in the estuarine Ría de Viga (NW Spain) during 3 years in two seasons.
the electrochemical speciation of metals in the Ría was dominated by organic matter, with the highest ligand concentration found for Cu.

the electrochemical speciation of Cu(II) and Zn(II) in the estuarine ecosystem Ría de Vigosurface and bottom waters can be successfully determined using SWASV and that two different ligands are involved in the complexation of Cu(II).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new methodological approach that can be applied to the study of metal speciation in natural waters.
the determination of metal speciation in the Ría of Vigo, an important estuary located in NW Spain, and the comparison of the different methods of data treatment.

the determination of metal speciation and the application of different methods to treat the voltammetric data in order to calculate the speciated concentrations of the metals in the Ria de Vigo estuarine ecosystem.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the most reliable results were obtained using Langmuir linear or Lorenzo nonlinear fits.
the Langmuir linear and non-linear fits, as well as the Lorenzo non-linear fits, are the most suitable methods for the speciation calculation of metals in the estuarine waters studied.
the speciation parameters calculated using the Lorenzo non-linear method and Langmuir fit for two ligand systems are the most reliable.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the Langmuir linear method was found to be the most suitable for the calculation of the speciation parameters, while the Lorenzo non-linear method was the most suitable for data treatment in the presence of a single ligand.
the use of the Langmuir linear and Lorenzo nonlinear fits are more suitable than Scatchard linear and Langmuir nonlinear fits for speciation calculations.
the Langmuir linear and Lorenzo non-linear methods can be considered the most suitable to obtain reliable speciation parameters for Cu, Pb and/or Zn in natural waters.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, for the studied system, the speciation parameters are reliable when the data treatment method is properly selected.
the use of the most suitable data treatment method for speciation calculations is crucial to obtain reliable results.

the use of the Lorenzo non-linear method to calculate the complex formation constant K' is recommended for samples in which complexation is high, while the Langmuir linear method can be used in samples with low or moderate complexation.
